desc: Ideation: each boundary k must be crossed at least c_k = #{j>k : P_j ≤ k} times; base = Σ k·c_k; total swap count parity must equal inversion parity, forcing an adjustment when Σ c_k ≢ inv (mod 2).

Found counterexample to naive "+1" adjustment: P=(1,4,3,2,5) → base 5, mismatch, but +1 at boundary 1 infeasible (c_1=0); hand-derived optimum 7 = base + min{k:c_k≥1}=2. Conjectured adjustment = min{k : c_k ≥ 1} (k=1 feasible iff c_1≥1 and N≥3; N=2 never has mismatch).
Fix brute force to proper Dijkstra (weighted edges make plain BFS invalid) — verifier code now uses heapq Dijkstra.
Run verifier for N=2..8 (46,233 permutations): 0 mismatches — formula base = Σ k·c_k plus adjustment min{k : c_k ≥ 1} on parity mismatch confirmed correct.
Finalize formula; implement O(N log N) solution (O(N) running count for c_k/base, BIT for inversion parity) with fast I/O.
Test final implementation on the three samples and edge cases (sorted, reverse-sorted, N=2 both orders, P_1=1 mismatch case (1,4,3,2,5) → 7) — all hand-traced through the exact algorithm and match.
Write final Python solution reading stdin, writing answer to stdout, enclosed in required delimiters.
